text:
sam: Noticed a weird UX/accessibility edge with our toasts + stacked modals in the console. Steps: open Project modal -> open Rename modal -> trigger a success toast while the Rename modal loads preview. Sometimes ESC closes both the toast and the Rename modal.

sam: Quick screencap in thread. Happens on Chrome, Firefox.

irene: Huh. Do our toasts get programmatic focus today? We set focus for screen reader announcement earlier.

sam: Yes, code calls `focus()` on the toast container so screen readers announce it, and we also add `role=\"alert\"`. But that shifts focus away from modal's form control.

leo: Using `role=\"alert\"` forces immediate announcement and might justify focus, but it should not move keyboard focus. Focus move + global ESC handler is probably the culprit.

nora: Agree. Two separate issues: (1) announcement strategy (alert vs status vs aria-live), (2) keyboard handling for ESC across layered UI.

irene: For a11y, `role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\"` is often better for non-critical success toasts so we don't interrupt keyboard users. Also keep a visible dismiss button that is tabbable.

leo: On ESC, our ModalStack registers `document.addEventListener('keydown', onEsc)` and closes the top modal when event.key === 'Escape' without checking `event.target` or `composedPath`. If the toast momentarily gets focus, ESC will bubble to ModalStack and close modal too.

sam: Repro shows toast gets focus for about 200ms while we call `announce()` then we blur back. If user hits ESC during that window, both close.

nora: Quick proposals: A) stop focusing toast container; rely on `aria-live` for SRs and only focus the dismiss button if user tabs; B) if keeping focus, change modal ESC handler to `if (event.defaultPrevented) return` and allow toast handler to call `event.stopPropagation()` when it handles ESC; C) debounce focus-restore so modal focus returns after toast lifecycle.

irene: My vote is A + small doc change: explain to devs that toasts announce via aria-live and only interactive controls are focusable. That follows best practices and reduces focus fights.

leo: Implementation nit: if we change to `role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\"`, make sure automated tests that assert SR output are updated. The previous test looked for focused element to confirm announcement which will break. Update a11y test harness to read container text instead.

sam: I'll prototype two branches: `toast-aria-live` (switch to polite + remove focus) and `esc-safeguard` (guard in ModalStack and add `event.defaultPrevented` checks).

qa-bot: new commit pushed to sam/toast-aria-live (d4e5f6). CI: accessibility checks updated.

nora: Can we add a tiny e2e: stacked modal -> trigger toast -> press ESC -> expect toast closed, modal still open. That should prevent regressions.

irene: Also add a note in components docs under Toaster: "Use aria-live for non-interruptive toasts; avoid programmatic focus on container; keep dismiss button tabbable."

leo: Heads-up to runtime folks: changing global ESC semantics may affect other flows (release notes). If we rely on global ESC in e.g. in-editor flows, test that behavior.

sam: I'll open PR with patch + unit + e2e tests. Assign @irene for a11y signoff and @nora for test review.

qa-bot: attaching failing test screenshot from prior run for reference.

sam: Thanks all. Will post PR link once ready.
